thread.title: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 pulls in from uncharted territory - MarketWatch

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 pulls in from uncharted territory - MarketWatch
text:
12:39 p.m. ET Share 
Focus: 10-year yield tags 45-month high, Apple retests major support, Intel takes flight, Latin American and Taiwan 
By Michael Ashbaugh Technicals columnist Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here. 
U.S. stocks are on the defensive, for a change, as an unusually strong month of January nears a conclusion. 
Against this backdrop, the big three U.S. benchmarks — S&P 500, Dow industrials and Nasdaq Composite — have dropped within view of near-term support, and the retests are worth tracking ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy directive, due out Wednesday. 
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.91% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks. 
As illustrated, the S&P has pulled in to first support (2,853) from record highs. 
With Tuesday’s firmly lower start, a near-term floor (2,830) is followed by firmer support matching the S&P’s breakout point, circa 2,807. 
Similarly, the Dow   has reversed from record territory. 
Tactically, its first notable floor matches the breakout point (26,150). 
Delving deeper, recall that the prevailing range bottom, circa 25,700, underpinned the Dow’s mid-January bearish reversal. 
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite has topped just above the 7,500 mark, an area defining range top. 
Conversely, near-term support (7,377) remains an inflection point. Tuesday’s early session low rests within three points. 
Widening the view to six months adds perspective. 
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has tagged the 7,500 mark, and pulled in from record territory. 
Though the nearly straightline January rally is longer-term bullish, near-term support remains poorly-defined. 
Tactically, the 20-day moving average, currently 7,272, is followed by support, circa 7,220, an area that underpinned the mid-month downturn. 
Similarly, the Dow   has knifed to record territory, and remains near-term extended. 
Here again, the 20-day moving average, currently 25,792, remains a relatively distant inflection point. The Dow has not closed lower since November. 
This is closely followed by the 25,700 support, an area better illustrated on the hourly chart. 
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has also reversed from its latest record high. 
Tactically, the 20-day moving average, currently 2,788, is rising toward near-term support. The S&P has registered just one close under the trending indicator since Aug. 29. The bigger picture 
The major U.S. benchmarks are on the defensive, for a change, as an unusually strong January nears a conclusion. 
On a headline basis, the Dow   is vying for its first consecutive triple-digit down days for the first time in nearly one year following the worst single session for U.S. stocks since September. 
Meanwhile, the CBOE Volatility Index VIX, +5.49% has tagged its highest print since August. 
So collectively, a consolidation phase has been long overdue — at least a sideways chopping-around period — and early signs are surfacing that one may be developing. 
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF has pulled in from record territory amid decreased volume. 
Recall that near-term support matches last week’s low (158.20) and is followed by a firmer floor (155.80) matching the key reversal (mid-month) low. 
Meanwhile, the S&P MidCap 400 has also pulled in amid lackluster volume. 
Tactically, a near-term floor matches last week’s low (359.20) and is followed by deeper support, circa 354.50, matching the mid-month low. Summing up the backdrop 
Collectively, potential cracks in the bull trend have surfaced, though limited true technical damage has thus far been inflicted. Still, the prevailing downturn, to the extent one takes hold, is in an admittedly early stage. 
Tactically, three S&P 500 support points stand out: S&P support matching the near-term breakout point, circa 2,807. The 20-day moving average, currently 2,788. S&P support closely matching the mid-month low, circa 2,774. 
As always, it’s the eventual retest — the response to support — that’s worth tracking. The S&P 500 has registered just one close under the 20-day moving average since Aug. 29, and a violation would mark a change in character. The prevailing bull trend, on balance, has been punctuated by successful retests of well-defined support 
Beyond near-term concerns, the S&P 500’s more important longer-term bias remains comfortably bullish pending a more technically aggressive downturn. 
The response to the State of the Union address, and likely more importantly, the Federal Reserve’s policy directive, due out Wednesday, should add color. 
See also: January breakout accelerates, S&P 500 clears 20-day volatility bands. Tuesday’s Watch List 
The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library. 
Drilling down further, investor concerns over rising interest rates have contributed to the prevailing broad-market downturn. 
Consider that the benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield TNX, +1.11% has reached a 45-month peak, its highest level since April 2014. The upturn originates from major support at 2.62, an area matching the former range top, illustrated on the six-month chart. 
On further strength, the yield’s next target rests at 3.04, a level matching the 2013 peak (3.036) and 2014 peak (3.034). An eventual close higher would punctuate a six-year peak, the yield’s highest level since July 2011. 
More broadly, the yield’s intermediate- to longer-term bias continues to point firmly higher. A violation of the breakout point (2.62) would place the brakes on yield bullish momentum. 
Moving to specific names, Dow 30 component Apple, Inc. AAPL, -0.95% has pulled in to a major technical test ahead of its quarterly results, due out Thursday. 
Significant support matches three inflection points: Support matching the former breakout point, the September peak of 164.94. Support matching the three-month range bottom, circa 166.50. The 100-day moving average, currently 166.80. 
Combined, Apple’s floor broadly spans from about 165.00 to 166.80, an area that is under siege early Tuesday. 
Against this backdrop, Apple’s relative strength index (not illustrated) has registered a four-month low, leaving it vulnerable to eventual downside follow-through. 
Based on today’s backdrop, Apple’s intermediate- to longer-term bias remains bullish, though the shares are tenuously positioned. The prevailing retest of support, and the response to Thursday’s earnings report, should add color. 
Tactically, a violation of the 165 area would mark a “lower low” (among other issues) raising a technical caution flag. 
Conversely, Intel Corp. INTC, -1.67% is a Dow 30 component taking flight. (Yield = 2.4%.) 
As illustrated, the shares have gapped to 17-year highs, clearing well-defined resistance after the company’s fourth-quarter results. 
The breakout resolves a double bottom, the “W” formation, defined by the December and January lows. 
Though near-term extended, and due to consolidate, the shares are attractive on a pullback. Support spans from about 47.60 to 48.10, levels matching the breakout point and the top of the gap. 
Looking elsewhere, the strong 2018 start has not been confined to the U.S. (Yield = 1.8%.) 
Technically, the iShares Latin American 40 ETF ILF, -0.67% has taken flight, knifing to three-year highs. A commodity-fueled resurgence, partly detailed last week, has contributed to the region’s breakout. 
Tactically, the nearly straightline January rally is longer-term bullish, and the shares are attractive on a pullback. Near-term support (37.80) is followed by the firmer beakout point (36.10). 
Similarly, the iShares Taiwan ETF EWT, -1.22% is acting well technically. (Yield = 1.9%.) 
Earlier this month, the shares knifed to all-time highs, clearing resistance matching the November peak. 
The ensuing bull flag is a continuation pattern, positioning the shares to build on the steep rally from the December low. Support broadly spans from about 37.80 to 38.40.
